description: Implementation of a high-performance timer management system with timer wheel, front-end and back-end communication channels, and timer lifecycle management.

classes.name: cmd_t
classes.description: Represents commands sent from front-end timers to the timer manager, including start, stop, create, destroy actions.

classes.name: timer_update_signaller
classes.description: Handles batching and signaling of timer update events from front-end to back-end.

classes.name: backend_channel
classes.description: Channel for communication between timer front-end and back-end, managing command buffers and signaling.

classes.name: frontend_handle
classes.description: Represents a timer instance on the front-end, managing timer state, callbacks, and communication with the backend.

classes.name: timer_manager::manager_impl
classes.description: Internal implementation of the timer manager, managing timers, wheel, and command processing.

classes.name: timer_handle
classes.description: Holds front-end and back-end context for each timer.

methods.name: handle_timer_commands
methods.description: Processes queued timer commands each tick.

methods.name: try_stop_timer_backend
methods.description: Attempts to stop a timer in the backend, handling expiry and callback dispatch.

methods.name: trigger_timeout_handling
methods.description: Dispatches timeout callback to the timer's executor if conditions are met.

methods.name: handle_postponed_timeouts
methods.description: Retries timeout callbacks that failed to dispatch previously.

methods.name: create_frontend_timer
methods.description: Creates or reuses a front-end timer handle for a new timer.

methods.name: tick
methods.description: Advances the timer system by one tick, processing expirations and commands.

methods.name: create_unique_timer
methods.description: Creates a new unique timer associated with a task executor.

methods.name: set
methods.description: Sets the timer duration and optional callback.
